result.note: Tests the June 2026 launch of the India–UK critical minerals observatory and the UK measures stalling CETA; skips Peter Kyle's comments on timelines.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the Critical Minerals Global Supply Chain Observatory (GSCO) launched in New Delhi in June 2026:
items: It is a joint initiative of IIT (ISM) Dhanbad, TEXMiN and the University of Cambridge.
It was first announced at the India–UK Prime Ministers' bilateral meeting in October 2025.
It was co-inaugurated by India's Minister of Coal and Mines and the UK Trade Minister.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 3 is wrong: the Observatory was co-inaugurated by G Kishan Reddy and UK Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper, not the Trade Minister. The platform monitors global critical mineral supply chains and was formalised by a Research Collaboration Agreement in March 2026.
questions.source: The Critical Minerals Global Supply Chain Observatory (GSCO) is a joint initiative of IIT (ISM) Dhanbad, TEXMiN, and the University of Cambridge.

questions.prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to the India–UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), as reported in June 2026:
items: Signing of the India–UK CETA — July 2025
Arrival of the UK Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism — 2027
Tightening of UK steel import quotas from 1 July 2026 — 30%
questions.ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explain: The third pair is wrong: UK steel import quotas are tightening by 60% from July 1, not 30%. India has signalled it may revisit Scotch whisky tariff concessions if these UK measures proceed.
questions.source: Two UK measures are the problem: steel import quotas tightening by 60% from July 1, and a Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism arriving in 2027.
